missionPremise: Plan row P-270 (OPS-16, added 2026-09-16, scope X2/X11): "every setback citation prints its effective date or a declared 'date unreadable' conflict." The operator's standing ruling (MOST-CURRENT SOURCE WINS, 2026-09-11) ends: "an unreadable date produces a conflict row with both values, never a silent pick." P-254 measured the defect at 29 of the 31 payloads that carry a setback citation at all, under two ids (XD-11 map/MCP, X11 LDT). This lane re-measured that population at source from the P-254 artifact and confirms it: `legsById` holds 52 subjects, 31 carry `envelopeCitationUrl`, 2 carry `envelopeCitationDate`, 29 do not.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate all of the following without me: (1) in each repo, ONE module owns the decision 'was this citation's effective date readable at source', and the three unreadable causes (absent at source / present but unparseable / never looked for) are three distinct machine-readable values, shown by a test that fails if any two are folded together; (2) a served citation whose date is unreadable carries a conflict row naming the source whose date could not be read AND the exact customer sentence, in a field the probe or a card reader can read, in both repos, byte-identical; (3) a citation whose date IS readable still serves it and prints it (the agreeing control), unchanged; (4) a parcel where two sources carry different dates still resolves to the more current one, unchanged, with the losing candidate disclosed; (5) no fallback that manufactures a date exists on either path — shown by a revert-and-run in both directions on the real pre-fix code; (6) the post-fix population is a measured count over the same 31 subjects, not an assertion, and the number of the 29 that become DATED (as opposed to DECLARED) is stated with the reason it is what it is.
scopeBasis: The build is the dispatch's items 1-5 in the one place each repo decides it, plus the honest measurement (item 6). Deliberately excluded, each with a reason: (a) ACQUIRING effective dates for the tables that lack them — that is the P-258 setback acquisition campaign and it is a source read, not a card fix; this lane makes the absence legible and unfabricatable instead, and says how many citations that leaves undated (see populationFact); (b) the MCP leg of XD-11 and the PDF leg — the dispatch names one PR per repo, and hauska-map and legacy-design-tools are the two repos named; the MCP (`artifacts/smartsite-mcp`) renders through LDT's own compose path, so the LDT half of this change reaches it, and the PDF's citation string is hauska-engine, which is not a repo this dispatch names; (c) any store write, deploy or merge (constraint); (d) adding a new `SetbackDateBasis` member to `@empressaio/setback-corpus/resolve` — it is a published npm package and this lane cannot publish; the three-state distinction is therefore built in-repo in each of the two repos on top of that package's existing `dateBasis` vocabulary, and promoting it into the package is named in leave_behind; (e) touching hauska-map/.github/workflows/** (P-318 holds it) and doc_repo/scripts/surface-probe.mjs (P-254 holds it); (f) Williamson 48491 in any store (constraint).

oneVocabularyModulePerRepo.contents: A pure, I/O-free module with (1) the type `SetbackDateReadState` = "read" | "unreadable-absent-at-source" | "unreadable-unparseable" | "unreadable-never-looked"; (2) `readSetbackDateAtSource(raw)` which takes the RAW value of the source's own date-bearing field (plus whether the key was present at all) and returns `{ sourceDate, state }` — strict `yyyy-mm-dd` only, no `Date.parse`, so `"2026-4-1"`, `"April 2026"`, `""`, a number and an object are all `unreadable-unparseable` rather than silently accepted; (3) `SETBACK_CITATION_VINTAGE_UNREADABLE_NOTE`, the ONE customer sentence; (4) `setbackCitationVintageRow(...)` returning the conflict row or null.
oneVocabularyModulePerRepo.whyDuplicatedRatherThanShared: The canon's 'one vocabulary module in the atom-contract package' cannot be satisfied from this lane: `@empressaio/atom-contract` (the PE app's dependency, 1.36.0) and `@empressaio/setback-corpus` (LDT's, 1.2.0) are published npm packages and this lane cannot publish. A byte-identical copy in each repo plus a test in EACH repo that pins the exact string and the exact type members is the strongest control available here — it makes drift a failing test rather than a silent difference — and promoting it into `@empressaio/atom-contract/display` is leave_behind item 1.

populationFact_statedBeforeBuilding: The dispatch asks what the 29-of-31 becomes, measured. The honest answer is known from the source read above and is pre-registered here so the post-fix measurement cannot be fitted to it: the number of DATED citations does not move. Sources carry no readable effective date for those 29, so no honest code can date them, and manufacturing one is the one outcome the dispatch forbids. What moves is the DECLARED population: 0 of 29 declared before, 29 of 29 declared after. The headline for the close is therefore '29 of 31 citations were served undated and undeclared; 29 of 29 are now served undated AND declared, 2 of 31 were dated and stay dated', and the count that does not move is stated with its reason rather than buried. The 2 dated subjects are the no-regression control.
knownHolesStatedNotDiscovered: The instrument cannot see the fix. P-254's `citationDatePresent` grades `citationUrl && !citationDate`, so a DECLARED undated citation still grades FAIL. The 29 count in a post-fix probe artifact will be unchanged until either the grader learns the declaration or the sources gain dates. This is a real limitation of the customer predicate and is leave_behind item 2; it is not worked around.

The string lives twice, once per repo, because the shared package cannot be published from this lane. The pinning tests are per-repo, so a future change to one copy that also updates its own test would still pass locally and diverge. Only the promotion into the package removes that.

hauska-map's `setbackSourceClause` (InspectCard.tsx) is a second place a citation is formatted; this lane routes the declared case around it, but the function still returns a bare citation for any caller that hands it a citation with no date and no state. Named, not deleted.

The atom-chain producer (`dm` block in atom-chain-to-facets.ts) can only declare `never-looked` or `unparseable`/`absent-at-source` to the extent `dm` carries a date basis at all; for a subject whose atom was minted before P-154 wave 6 there is no basis on the wire and the honest state is `never-looked`. Which of the 29 fall in that class is NOT separable from the served payload alone, so the per-subject classification in the measurement harness is derived from the module that produced each subject's citation, and is stated as a derivation with its basis rather than as a per-parcel fact.

LDT's `dateBasis` vocabulary is owned by a published package whose `"unreadable"` member the new three states refine. A caller that reads only `dateBasis` still cannot tell which of the three happened; callers must read the new field. Stated, not fixed.
The Pflugerville vendored-table drift (hauska-map's copy lacks the P-258 CL3/CL4/CL5 addendum LDT's copy has) is reported and untouched.
